item.title: Trump claims Iran is exploring chemical, biological weapons
item.description:
Trump claims Iran is exploring chemical, biological weapons

US President Donald Trump claimed that Iran is seeking to look into chemical and biological weapons.

Trump said that Tehran was "looking at gases, looking at bio" during an interview with Fox News, without providing evidence to back his claims. 

The American president also said that while he does not believe Iran would launch a possible attack on Washington, he vowed that there would be retaliation if one occurred, saying: "If it does happen, we wipe them out."

item.description:
Saudi Arabia says danger in Wadi Al Dawasir, As Sulayyil passed after warning issued

Saudi Arabia’s civil defence said that danger in Wadi Al Dawasir and As Sulayyil governorates passed, shortly after it issued alerts over a potential threat. 

They urged residents to follow authorities instructions and avoid gathering and filming.

This brings the number of security alerts in the kingdom within the past few hours to a total of five.

item.title: Apec summit as it happened: Xi welcomes Trump on China visit as Putin claims Europe in ‘humiliating decline’
item.description:
This blog is now closed, you can read more on this story here

Yalta became a byword for betrayal. Will Trump, Xi and Putin enact another carve-up?

That is the question the Guardian’s diplomatic correspondent Patrick Wintour seeks to address in his piece about the expected, Putin, Trump and Xi, meeting at Apec on Thursday.

It is a truism in diplomacy that if you are not around the table, the risk is that you, or your values, are on the menu and about to be carved up. Many excluded from the summit in Shenzhen, principally Ukraine but also eastern Europe and Baltic countries, Taiwan and even Iran, have reason to be nervous that their sponsors might abandon them in a complex geopolitical trade-off that Putin envisions, and Trump seems to endorse.

Asif Merchant, who had alleged ties to Iran, sought to hire a hitman to assassinate a politician or a government official in the United States, a Brooklyn court found.
